d: How the Nostr Vault wallet works: connect a Lightning wallet with a Nostr Wallet Connect (NWC) link, turn on zap buttons, disconnect, and the on-chain Bitcoin address under Advanced.
h: What the wallet is · Connect a wallet · Turning on zap buttons · Saving the wallet to your Nostr account · Disconnecting · Bitcoin On-Chain · The Wallet Connect tutorial
x: The basics What the wallet is A zap is a small bitcoin tip sent over Lightning (bitcoin's fast payment network) to the person who posted. Amounts are in sats , the smallest unit of bitcoin. Nostr Vault never holds that money. Your sats stay in a Lightning wallet you run somewhere else, such as Alby Hub, Coinos, Primal or Zeus. Nostr Wallet Connect (NWC) is a standard way for an app to ask that wallet to pay. Your wallet gives you a link that starts with nostr+walletconnect:// , and you paste it into Nostr Vault. Treat the link like cash. Anyone who has it can spend from that wallet. If your wallet lets you, make a connection with a spending limit just for Nostr Vault. Step by step Connect a wallet In your wallet app, find Nostr Wallet Connect (NWC) and copy the connection link. In Nostr Vault, open Settings → Account → Wallet . Paste the link into the Wallet Connect box (on Android it's called Nostr Wallet Connect (NWC) ). On the web, tap Connect wallet . The app pastes the link only. There is no QR scanner for it. Once a wallet is connected you'll see its Balance and can set your Default Zap (on Android, Default Zap Amount (sats) ), the amount one tap sends. On iPhone, iPad, Mac and Android you can also start from your own profile. Tap the bolt, labelled Lightning . With no wallet yet, it shows No Wallet Connected and a Connect a wallet button that takes you to the same place. On Android the wallet is on the Settings tab of that screen. Once connected, the Lightning screen shows your balance and lets you receive with an invoice, pay an invoice, lightning address or LNURL, and see your history if your wallet shares it. Opt in Turning on zap buttons Zap buttons on posts are a choice you make under Settings → Appearance → Post buttons . Add ⚡️ in the Add ⚡️ field to show a zap button, and remove it to hide the button. Zapping someone from their profile is always available. iPhone, iPad and Mac: the zap button is off until you add ⚡️. It then shows on posts, live streams and locked articles. Android: ⚡️ is there by default, so posts show a zap button until you remove it. Web: notes show a zap button. A tap sends your default zap, and holding it lets you pick another amount. Each zap goes straight from your wallet to the author. Nostr Vault takes no cut. Phones and Mac Saving the wallet to your Nostr account On iPhone, iPad, Mac and Android, the Wallet page can switch on Save wallet to my Nostr account . The link is then stored encrypted to your key on your relays, so Nostr Vault on your other devices (or the Wisp app) can pick it up with Use saved wallet . Anyone who has your Nostr key can read it and spend from the wallet. Remove from my account takes it off again. Stop using it Disconnecting iPhone, iPad, Mac and Android: delete the link from the Wallet Connect box. If you saved it to your account, also tap Remove from my account . Web: tap Disconnect wallet , then Disconnect . The web app keeps the link only in that browser, and deletes it when you sign out. To be sure the app can't spend any more, also revoke the connection in your wallet app. Advanced Bitcoin On-Chain Separate from Lightning, the apps can make a regular bitcoin address from your Nostr key. It lives under Settings → Advanced → Bitcoin On-Chain on iPhone, iPad, Mac and Android. It isn't in the web app. Turn on Bitcoin Address to see the address and a QR code, and use Copy Address to share it. Sweep Wallet sends everything at that address to another address you choose. This one is different. Bitcoin sent to this address is controlled by your Nostr key, so anyone with your key can spend it. Before a sweep, the app warns you not to send to a hardware wallet or an exchange: that would tie your npub to that wallet on the public blockchain, and it can't be undone. d: How Nostr Vault's mesh works: your phone or Mac serves your own photos over the FIPS mesh, with no public IP, domain or cloud. My Devices, kiosk mode, share pages and privacy.
h: What the mesh is · Your phone or Mac as your photo server · My Devices · Kiosk mode · Share pages · Privacy · What's live vs what's in 3.0
x: The basics What the mesh is Most phones and home computers can't be reached from the internet. They sit behind a home router, move between Wi-Fi and cell, and have no fixed address. That's why your photos normally live on someone else's server. FIPS is a mesh network where you reach a device by its Nostr key (an npub) instead of an IP address. It works across home routers and mobile networks, and the connection between two devices is encrypted end to end. Nostr Vault uses it to let your devices reach each other, and to let other people fetch your photos from you. Photos stay trustworthy no matter who hands them over. On Nostr, a photo is named by its fingerprint (a hash). Whoever sends it, the app checks the fingerprint, and if it matches, it's the photo. If it doesn't, the photo is thrown away and loaded the normal way. Your own server Your phone or Mac as your photo server Your Nostr profile already keeps a list of where your media lives. Nostr Vault adds one more entry to that list: your own device, written as its mesh address. It goes after your normal media servers, so apps that don't know about the mesh carry on as before. An app that does know about it can ask your device for a photo directly, by its fingerprint, the same way it would ask any media server. Your photos still go to your normal servers too. Your device is one more place they can come from, and the one you own. On a Mac , the Nostr Vault app serves while it's open. Leave it running and your Mac is an always-on photo server. On a phone , it serves while the app is open, or full-time in kiosk mode on a spare phone. To turn it on, open Settings → Mesh → FIPS Mesh and switch on Mesh . Serving is off until you turn it on. Your devices, together My Devices My Devices is the list of your own phones, Macs, home vault and browser page that reach each other over the mesh. Devices on this list sync with each other in full: your notes, your photos and your history. On each device, open Settings → Mesh → FIPS Mesh , turn on Mesh , and in This Device tap Copy . That's the device's mesh address. On your other devices, go to My Devices → Add a device by address , paste it, and pick what it is: Vault on Mac , Phone or Home vault . Do it in both directions: add each phone on the Mac, and the Mac on each phone. A device on the list shows a dot when it's in reach. To check that everything arrived, use FIPS Mesh → Sync → Check sync on a phone. An always-on vault Kiosk mode Kiosk mode turns a phone into a small always-on vault. Put an old phone on a charger at home, turn kiosk mode on under Share With Others , and it keeps serving. It keeps the screen on, so the phone keeps serving. Leaving the app pauses kiosk mode, and it turns on again when you come back. Your own devices in My Devices reach it in full. Everyone else can only read the photos in your posts, and only slowly: 1 MB/s shared between all of them, at most 256 MB each, and 1 GB per session before they have to wait. They can't read your notes or change anything. You can also limit who can view to only your own devices. Set another phone to use it as its Home vault , and your new notes and photos go to the kiosk phone over the mesh, which sends your notes on to your relays. Works in any browser Share pages When you share a post from Nostr Vault, the link opens that post in the Nostr Vault web app, in any normal browser. Anyone can read it as a guest, with no account and nothing to install, and sign in from there to reply or like. If a photo in that post or its replies can't be loaded from its usual server, the browser fetches it from that author's own device over the mesh. It joins the mesh for that one visit with a throwaway key, asks the device for the photo by its fingerprint, checks the fingerprint, and shows it. The photo is fetched by the visitor's own browser. nostrvault.app keeps no copy of it, and a guest's browser keeps nothing once the tab is closed. You may see blob:https://nostrvault.app/ as the image addr

d: The Nostr Vault browser relay at nostrvault.app/relay/: a browser tab that keeps your notes and serves them to your own devices over the FIPS mesh. Pairing, Start FIPS, the screensaver, My Devices and limits.
h: What the browser relay is · Pair your iPhone with the page · What it keeps and serves · The screensaver · When the tab closes · In My Devices · Limits and privacy
x: The basics What the browser relay is A relay is a server that stores Nostr notes and hands them out. The browser relay is one that runs inside a web page, at nostrvault.app/relay/ . It stores notes in the browser's own storage on that device and joins the FIPS mesh, so your own devices can reach it by its key. New to the mesh? Read The mesh first. The page keeps no Nostr key of yours. Your notes arrive already signed, and the page checks each signature. A good spot for it is an old phone or tablet on a charger. Set it up Pair your iPhone with the page On your iPhone, open FIPS Mesh and turn the mesh on. Under This Device , tap Copy . That's the phone's mesh address. On the device that will run the page, open nostrvault.app/relay/ . Paste the address into the box under the FIPS heading (one address per line) and tap Save owners . The page reloads. Tap Start FIPS . The status shows the page's own mesh address . Copy it. On the iPhone, go to My Devices → Add a device by address , paste the page's address, and pick Browser page . The phone then connects for the page. If it doesn't, open the page's entry in My Devices and tap Connect this phone . Copy this phone's mesh address is there too. A link of the form nostrvault.app/relay/#owner=npub1 also adds an owner. The page asks you to confirm each address first, because an owner can write to the page and read everything on it. Only accept your own. What it does What it keeps and serves Your new notes. While the iPhone app is open, each new note you post also goes to the page. Send my latest notes sends your 20 most recent notes from the phone. The result line says how many the page kept. In this testing build, check that number: if it says 0 kept, the page did not take your notes. Checked notes only. The page checks each note's signature and turns away notes from authors it isn't set up for. Owners only. The page serves notes on the mesh only to the addresses saved as owners. Anyone else's connection is dropped without an answer. Photos, read only. Under Show photo , you can paste a photo's fingerprint (sha256) or a .fips link and the page fetches it from a paired vault. It shows the photo only if the fingerprint matches. Photos aren't stored on the page. The page reaches your phone through the public mesh entry points (seeds). Once both ends are connected it tries a direct link. On the iPhone, leave the middle server under Advanced on its public setting. With None , a browser page only connects on the same network. Keep it awake The screensaver Start screensaver fills the screen with a black "relay running" view: a count, the uptime, whether the screen is kept awake (the wake lock), and whether the seed is up. Tap anywhere to leave it. After a reload, start it again. The count on this screen is the page's own test notes, not your notes. Report shows storage, uptime gaps and a signature self-test, if you want the details. When it stops When the tab closes The relay only runs while the page is open and the screen is on. Closed, locked or in the background, nothing reaches it. Notes the phone sends while the page is down are not queued. Tap Send my latest notes once it's back. Stored notes stay in the browser and are there when you reopen the page. Tap Start FIPS again; it doesn't start by itself. Stop FIPS takes the page off the mesh. The page's mesh key lives in the browser's site data. Clear that data and the page gets a new address, so pair it again. Your devices list In My Devices The page shows up in My Devices as a Browser page , the role whose job reads "Gets your new notes while this app is open." You can have one browser page per account; adding a new one replaces the old. To stop sending, open its entry and tap Remove from my devices . Anything already on the page stays there. Android and Mac also offer Browser page under My Devices → Add a device by address . In this build, only the iPhone app sends notes to the page. Be candid Limits and privacy The tab must stay open. d: Media servers (Blossom) in Nostr Vault: where photos go when you post, adding and removing servers, mirroring copies back to your device, the Media & Cache settings, and uploading from the share sheet.
h: What a media server is · Where a photo goes when you post · Add or remove a media server · Mirroring · Media & Cache · Uploading from the share sheet · Your device as a photo server
x: The basics What a media server is Relays only carry text. A photo or video is too big for that, so it goes to a media server instead, and your note holds a link to it. Nostr media servers speak a shared language called Blossom , so any Nostr app can read from them. A photo on a Blossom server is named by its fingerprint (a hash of the file). The same photo has the same name on every server, so it can be copied between servers and still be checked. Your account publishes a list of your media servers. Other apps read that list to find your files. When you post Where a photo goes when you post The app first saves the photo on this device, in your vault. It then uploads it to all of your outside media servers at once. As soon as one of them has it, the note is sent. The other servers keep uploading in the background. If no outside server takes the photo, the post is not lost. It waits under Settings → Media Servers in Waiting to send , and sends itself when a server answers. Tap Try sending now to retry straight away. Posting a photo still needs a public media server. A photo that is only on your phone can't be seen by anyone else, so the app won't post it without an outside server. Your list Add or remove a media server Open Settings → Media Servers . It sits in the Relays group, under Relays. Add: type the server's address (for example blossom.example.com ) in the box and tap the add button next to it. If you leave out https:// , the app adds it. Remove: tap the red button next to a server (a minus sign on iPhone and Mac, a bin on Android). Each change is saved and your updated list is published to your relays. If you set up Sync with Vault on Mac , your Mac is used as a media server too. It shows at the top of the page and you don't need to add it by hand. In the web app , the same page is Settings → Media Servers . Use Add and Remove , then Save and publish . Test checks that a saved server answers. The web app uploads to the server marked first first. If you have never published a list, it starts from two default servers. It also needs at least one server in the list. There is no button to reorder servers. In the web app, a server you add goes to the end of the list. Copies you own Mirroring Mirroring brings your own photos back from your media servers into your vault on this device, so they work offline and you keep a copy if a server goes away. Both controls are on the Media Servers page: Mirror Now downloads your media from your outside servers to this device, once. It shows progress while it runs. Auto-Mirror Media keeps doing it for you. Other people's photos Media & Cache When you look at photos and videos in the feed, the app keeps temporary copies so they load faster next time. You control this in Settings → Media & Cache , in the Feed & Display group. The web app doesn't have this page. Autoplay Videos plays videos as you scroll. Prefetch Profile Pictures loads profile pictures ahead of time for smoother scrolling. Disable Media Cache stops saving copies, so media downloads again each time. Keep Media For sets how long copies are kept: 1, 3, 7, 14 or 30 days, or Never. Clear Media Cache deletes the temporary copies to free space. Your vault and your media servers are not touched. On Android there is one more switch, Use Local Blossom Cache . It loads media through a Blossom cache app on the same phone, when one is running. Uploads never go through it. From other apps Uploading from the share sheet You can send photos and videos to Nostr Vault from your gallery or any other app, using the system share button. The two phones handle it differently: Phone What happens Android Pick Nostr Vault in the share sheet. The upload to Blossom starts straight away, one file at a time, with a notification while it runs. iPhone Pick Nostr Vault, then tap Add to Blossom upload queue . The files are added to a queue. Open Nostr Vault or tap its notification to finish the upload. On iPhone the upload happens in the app, not in the shar

d: Nostr Vault release notes for iPhone, Mac and Android: 3.0.0 (in testing) with the FIPS mesh, and the 2.7.2 builds you can download today.
x: Build 41 · iPhone, Mac and Android 3.0.0 In testing 3.0 is in testing and not released yet. The apps you can download today are 2.7.2. Nostr Vault 3.0 connects your own devices directly over the FIPS mesh , with no server in between. Your devices, connected. Turn on FIPS Mesh in Settings and add your devices by address or QR code. On Android you can add your Mac, your other phones or a home vault. See My Devices . iPhone and Mac: the mesh engine runs inside the Mac app, so there is nothing else to install. The Mac serves your photos to your own devices, and your public photos to anyone else who asks. See your own photo server . Notes and photos to your Mac. Add your Mac as Vault on Mac and each new note and photo goes to it over the mesh. Your notes and history also sync back from the Mac. iPhone and Mac: Check sync with Vault on Mac now ends on "Done" with counts, or says why it stopped. Home vault. A spare phone can be your home vault. It gets your new posts and media and passes them on. See kiosk mode . Photos over the mesh. Photos kept on your devices load over the mesh in the feed, the Vault and profiles. Your address stays private. Once you add a device, only your devices learn this phone's address. Anyone else gets public photos only. On Android, that is up to the limit you set under Pause after . See privacy . Android: if the mesh was on, it starts again with the relay when the phone restarts. Fixes iPhone: the phone ran hot with the app open. The relay now gets memory sized to the phone. iPhone and Mac: search no longer freezes while you type a common word. Android: on some phones the app ran out of memory and closed when a long note full of links was in the feed. Posting a photo still needs a public media server. Build 40 · iPhone, Mac and Android 2.7.2 (build 40) iPhone and Mac. This is the App Store build. The app now stays cool with it open all day. The relay pauses work nobody can see while the app is in the background, and backs off from flaky relays and signers. The Web of Trust globe draws more cheaply. On the iPhone, a locked article no longer links out to buy it on Fanfares. The Mac keeps that link. On both, it can only point at the article itself. New Message from a profile keeps the person you picked. Android. Android now looks and acts like the iPhone app. Messages and notifications, Settings, the tab bar, setup, profiles, search, follow lists, the Web of Trust globe, the feed, note details and the composer have all been matched to the iPhone. The app runs cooler. The relay pauses work nobody can see while the app is in the background, and backs off from flaky relays. A crash at launch on a new install is fixed. Build 39 · iPhone, Mac and Android 2.7.2 (build 39) iPhone and Mac. The App Store release candidate. Your keys and settings are safer. The config file is written in one go, backed up, and never reset by a damaged copy. Imported keys are checked. Fanfares articles get Open in Fanfares and Already unlocked? . The app itself never pays. Recipes, streams, articles and profiles can be opened in the rest of Nostr. Zaps on posts, live streams and articles are opt-in on the Mac, as on the iPhone. The on-chain wallet moves to Settings → Advanced . Highlights and comments from people you blocked no longer show under articles. iPad fixes for the relay card, the tour card and the Media viewer. Android. The App Store review pass for Android. Reposts, deletes, profile edits and follow-list changes are signed only as the account they belong to. Switching accounts can't carry one account's follow list into another. Settings are saved in one go and survive a damaged file. The owner key moves out of the config file, and a broken credential store no longer crashes the app. Notes backup works. Fanfares articles can be unlocked with a zap from the lock card. Other locked articles stay locked. Recipes, streams, articles and profiles can be opened in the rest of Nostr. Global shows a new account's web. Copying your nsec

t: Build the mesh into your client
d: How another Nostr client can read photos over the FIPS mesh: the fipsmesh:// address form in kind 10063, plain Blossom GETs, and the NIP-F1 draft.
x: The mesh address is one new entry form, fipsmesh://<npub>/ , in lists you already use: the media server list ( kind:10063 ) and, later, the relay list ( kind:10002 ). No new event kinds. Requests are plain Blossom GET /<sha256> , with the same hash check. A client that doesn't know the form skips it and carries on with the other servers in the list. A client that does can ask the device for the photo by its fingerprint, the same way it asks any media server, and throws the photo away if the fingerprint doesn't match. Draft, not yet submitted NIP-F1: Nostr over the FIPS Mesh The address form, transport, safety rules for serving and reading, and where Nostr Vault implements each part. Read the draft → How it works for people using the app is on The mesh .
